title: Swiftline Components Ltd goes public
body: Swiftline Components Ltd, a public company, received its Certificate of Incorporation in April. To build a new plant it decided to raise Rs 50 crore from the public by issuing equity shares. It obtained SEBI approval for the issue and filed a copy of its prospectus with the Registrar of Companies. Bankers were appointed to collect the application money and brokers were engaged to distribute application forms. Because the directors expected a strong response, the company did not appoint any underwriters. It applied to one recognised stock exchange for permission to deal in its shares, and the permission arrived four weeks after the subscription list closed. When the list closed, applications had been received for shares worth 92 per cent of the issue size. Before shares were allotted, the finance manager suggested using part of the application money lying with the bankers to pay some urgent bills of machinery suppliers, arguing that the money would belong to the company anyway once the shares were allotted.
